However, while the magnitude of L-LIP is unchanged, it is possible that I-LTP is qualitatively different in its requirement for new protein synthesis when FMRP is absent, as is the case for mGluR-LTD (and LTPI priming, see below). Therefore, it will be important to test the protein synthesis-dependency of L-ITP in FarI KO mice to show that FMP truly does not play a role in regulating the persistence of LTP. Alternatively, FMP may be required for the regulation of local but not somatic translation in the context of L-LTP (Figure IC).
